- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods, especially when sentiment > 0.5 and recent prices are rising.
- Underestimate prices after sharp spikes or when sentiment drops below 0.3 — model tends to overreact to recent highs.
- Correct for mean reversion: if forecast is > 10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- Lag correction: if sentiment is positive but forecast is still high, subtract 1–2% per day of lagged sentiment decay.
- Avoid over-optimism in 30-day forecasts — especially when sentiment is high but recent price action is trending down.
- When sentiment is low (<0.2) and price is falling, model often undercorrects — add 1–3% to forecast to account for downward momentum.
- Don’t assume sentiment directly drives price — if sentiment is high but price is flat or falling, reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overconfidence.
